title: 1980 AHSME Problem 10
statement: The number of teeth in three meshed circular gears \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) are \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z,\) respectively. (The teeth on all gears are the same size and regularly spaced as in the figure.) The angular speeds, in revolutions per minute, of \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) are in the proportion

solutions.text:
The gears’ circumferences are proportional to \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z,\) while their tangential speeds have equal magnitude. Their angular speeds are therefore proportional to \[ \frac1x:\frac1y:\frac1z. \] Multiplying all three terms by \(xyz\) gives \(yz:xz:xy.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Meshed teeth have the same tangential speed at their points of contact
Angular speed is inversely proportional to circumference and hence to the number of teeth
